transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Linda Gomez (CISO - Springfield Bank), Tom Reed (Lead SRE), Priya Nayar (Compliance)

Summary (auto): Weekly pilot security check-in focused on SSO, audit logs, SOC2 evidence, KMS, and VPC connectivity.

[00:00:05] Aaron Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Linda Gomez: Linda here, CISO for Springfield.
[00:00:15] Tom Reed: Tom, SRE.
[00:00:18] Priya Nayar: Priya, compliance.
[00:00:22] Maya Patel: Maya from Redwood, SE on the POC.
[00:00:26] Aaron Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda — SSO status, audit logs + retention, SOC2 docs, KMS questions, and next steps.
[00:00:40] Linda Gomez: We pushed SSO with our IdP last week, had some metadata mismatch. Wanted to validate the SAML metadata you sent.
[00:00:50] Maya Patel: Right, I saw that too; looks like the ACS URL had a trailing slash in your metadata which our test IdP didn't like. We updated on our side and pushed an alternate ACS endpoints list.
[00:01:05] Tom Reed: When you say alternate endpoints, is that the hosted redirect or the VPC endpoint for private deployment?
[00:01:12] Maya Patel: The one we updated is the hosted redirect for the hosted POC env. If you plan to use Private (VPC) later we'll provide a different ACS and certificate.
[00:01:22] Linda Gomez: For compliance we need SAML assertions to include email and employee id attribute; can you confirm Redwood consumes those?
[00:01:30] Maya Patel: Yes we map email and uid by default; you can customize attributes. I'll include the mapping in the SSO doc.
[00:01:40] Aaron Chen: Action: Maya will share SAML metadata and a step-by-step guide.
[00:01:45] [crosstalk]
[00:01:48] Priya Nayar: Also on retention — we have 7 years for certain logs per bank policy. Is that supported or will logs be offloaded to our storage?
[00:01:58] Maya Patel: Our hosted offering keeps audit logs for 90 days by default; for longer-term retention we offer log export to customer S3 or can be integrated with your SIEM. For Private deployments you keep full control of retention.
[00:02:12] Tom Reed: We'll probably want log export to our S3 and then lifecycle rules on your side or ours? Ideally our side.
[00:02:20] Aaron Chen: We can support push to your S3 with kms-encrypted transfer; Maya will document the export pipeline and sample schema.
[00:02:30] Maya Patel: I'll include the audit log schema sample — note that some field names in our runtime are abbreviated, transcription sometimes shows KVcache as KV cache so names may differ.
[00:02:40] Linda Gomez: About SOC 2 evidence — can you share the latest report and scope? We need to check controls for encryption, access logs, and change management.
[00:02:50] Aaron Chen: Sure. We'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and the scope doc; also include recent penetration test summary.
[00:02:58] Priya Nayar: Are your encryption keys customer-managed? We prefer CMK in our KMS for production.
[00:03:05] Maya Patel: For hosted customers we offer an option to integrate your KMS for key wrapping (bring-your-own-key). For Dedicated/Private, you can host keys in your KMS or HSM. There's some engineering lead time for full BYOK, but it's supported.
[00:03:20] Tom Reed: Network-wise, for the VPC option, what's the expected connectivity test? Do you do an on-prem tunnel, direct peer, or is it customer-initiated?
[00:03:30] Aaron Chen: We support VPC peering and private link style connections; for on-prem we typically do a site-to-site VPN or direct connect. For the POC we can run a simple connectivity bench to validate throughput and latency.
[00:03:44] Tom Reed: Good — let's schedule that next week. We'll need IP allowlist and port info.
[00:03:50] Maya Patel: I'll send the network checklist. Also a note: some customers name the model runtime differently in docs — e.g., Redwood runtime vs redwood-infer — so check the endpoints list.
[00:04:05] Linda Gomez: Any data residency constraints we should be aware of? We have EU accounts and some customer data that must stay in the EU.
[00:04:12] Aaron Chen: We can pin regions for hosted, and for Private you can deploy in your region. We'll confirm the region options for your regulated workloads.
[00:04:22] Priya Nayar: For auditability, do you provide immutable audit logs with tamper-evidence or just event exports?
[00:04:30] Maya Patel: Hosted audit logs are write-once via an append-only stream internally, and we publish hash chaining for tamper-evidence on request — typically enterprise add-on. Exports to customer S3 can then be locked with retention policies.
[00:04:45] Aaron Chen: Competitors mentioned — BigCloudAI had similar features but with higher latency on our internal benchmarks; ModelServeCo offers a BYO infra approach. We discussed tradeoffs earlier in the POC.
[00:04:55] Tom Reed: For the audit log schema, can you include an example of a user action versus system action?
[00:05:02] Maya Patel: Absolutely — I'll include example events: user.login, user.token.rotate, model.invoke, cache.evict, and internal.scale.
[00:05:12] [pause]
[00:05:20] Aaron Chen: Quick sync on permissioning — RBAC is available, with roles and OAuth/SSO mapping. You can mirror LDAP groups into roles.
[00:05:30] Linda Gomez: We need admin separation for ops and compliance, and stricter controls on model rollback. Can we get logs tied to deploy IDs?
[00:05:38] Maya Patel: Yes, each deploy and rollout has an ID and we correlate it in audit logs; we'll show you a sample in the doc.
[00:05:48] Priya Nayar: On legal / data processing addendum — we need a DPA and clarity on subprocessors.
[00:05:55] Aaron Chen: We'll attach the DPA and list of subprocessors in the follow-up packet.
[00:06:02] Tom Reed: Any sandbox for running evals without sending live data? We want to run a small set of customer prompts.
[00:06:08] Maya Patel: We have a masked-data sandbox and a local offline option for Private. For the POC you can redact or token-hash inputs and we can run with that.
[00:06:18] Linda Gomez: Great. For the SSO test, can you create an IdP test account for our team?
[00:06:24] Maya Patel: We'll provide an IdP test flow and sample accounts; but usually customers configure in their IdP and then we validate. I'll include a checklist.
[00:06:34] Aaron Chen: Let's talk timelines and deliverables: Maya sends SAML metadata and network checklist by tomorrow; Aaron sends SOC2 and pentest by Friday; Tom will export sample audit logs by next Tuesday; Priya to confirm retention policy by next Thursday.
[00:06:48] Priya Nayar: Sounds good.
[00:06:50] [15:00 mark — mid meeting notes omitted for brevity]
[00:20:10] Tom Reed: One more question on tokenization — does Redwood store raw prompts or only a hashed/processed form? We need to ensure PHI is not retained.
[00:20:20] Maya Patel: By default we store full request payloads for troubleshooting for 90 days; for regulated data we can enable masking or send tokens to your S3 with no retention on hosted. For Private deployments you control storage.
[00:20:35] Linda Gomez: We'll aim to use masking during POC and decide on retention later.
[00:20:40] Aaron Chen: Noted.
[00:20:44] Maya Patel: I'll add configuration flags for input redaction in the doc and include an example config snippet.
[00:20:52] Aaron Chen: Any blockers on your side for the planned VPC bench?
[00:20:57] Tom Reed: Need IP ranges and an auth token; also our networking team wants to do a dry run.
[00:21:05] Maya Patel: I'll send the IP allowlist and port requirements.
[00:21:12] Linda Gomez: For SOC2 evidence, do you provide system config snapshots?
[00:21:17] Aaron Chen: We can provide configuration exports and change control logs for the period in scope.
[00:21:24] Priya Nayar: Okay, on next steps we'll also request a short meeting with your security engineering to review the pentest findings.
[00:21:32] Aaron Chen: We'll set that up.
[00:21:36] [closing]
[00:21:38] Aaron Chen: Recap: Maya send SAML and audit schema, Aaron send SOC2 & pentest, Tom send sample logs, Priya confirm retention. Schedule VPC bench next week. Anything else?
[00:21:50] Linda Gomez: No, that's it. Thanks.
[00:21:53] Tom Reed: Thanks all.
[00:21:55] Maya Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
